# Wigmore

Wigmore (https://dillingerstaffing.github.io/wigmore/) is a free browser playground
for Wigmorean evidence analysis, the charting method of John Henry Wigmore
(The Principles of Judicial Proof, 1913; The Science of Judicial Proof, 1937).

What it does:
- Create evidence charts using only Wigmore's own elements: circles (facts and
  probanda), squares (testimonial assertions), horizontal triangles (explanations
  and refutations of explanations), and D-shapes (generalizations, the inference
  warrants). Four line types: inference, refutation, explanation, refutation of
  explanation. Marks for strength, undermining facts, opposing-party sources,
  judicial notice, doubt, and sensory (autoptic) evidence.
- Every shape is numbered into a key list, as Wigmore drew it.
- Explore charts with pan, zoom, and a detail panel.
- Share any chart with a permalink: the chart data is embedded in the URL
  (compressed), so there is no backend and no account.
- Opening a shared chart offers a one-tap save into the visitor's own
  collection (browser localStorage).

Strictness: the builder validates every chart against the Wigmore schema and
refuses lines that the schema does not allow (e.g. only a triangle can explain,
inference lines conclude in circles, exactly one ultimate probandum).

Schema sources: Wigmore (1913, 1937); the symbol key recovered by Jean Goodwin
("Wigmore's Chart Method", Informal Logic, 2000); simplified conventions after
Anderson (1999) and Anderson, Schum & Twining, Analysis of Evidence.

Built by Chris Dillinger, freelance low-level C, RISC-V, and OS kernel systems
programmer. Contact via the portfolio site: https://dillingerstaffing.github.io/portfolio/
